summary: This remains the correct architecture and now handles Git object formats and unattended model selection more thoughtfully, but it still carries unresolved transport and verification defects from the previous round. Stalled-prompt recovery can duplicate delivered work, compact interactive support is declared without a combined review-shaped fixture, verbatim relay remains undefined across terminal normalization, and recent successful session history is not a specified or reliable route-readiness source. These are narrow changes rather than a redesign, but they are load-bearing enough to block adoption.

blocking_findings.description: The retry decision still relies on whether the prompt is visible in recent rendered output, which does not prove delivery or non-delivery and can duplicate a completed turn.
blocking_findings.required_change: Base recovery on pre/post state_change_seq and known input-ready state; any ambiguous delivery becomes transport UNKNOWN rather than a resend.

blocking_findings.description: The 180-line support claim has not been demonstrated for a combined real-review scenario with tool calls, repaint and a compact final verdict, and rendered-line count depends on pane geometry.
blocking_findings.required_change: Define logical-line and minimum-geometry constraints and require a provider-specific combined review fixture before marking Claude or Codex interactive review supported.

blocking_findings.description: Recent successful session history is undefined as a data source and does not prove current authentication, launch posture, subscription readiness or route quality. Catalog absence is also not clearly distinguished from model absence.
blocking_findings.required_change: Use a deterministic policy based on saved validated selection plus current posture/auth/catalog evidence; define transient catalog failure separately and do not consult unspecified private session history.

blocking_findings.description: Findings delivered without changes is not testable until the design defines how Herdr soft-wrap and text normalization affect the payload.
blocking_findings.required_change: Define verbatim as complete, ordered, unedited Unicode Markdown after documented Herdr normalization and test that invariant.

blocking_findings.description: The bundle design still omits exact dependency versions, lockfile policy and preservation of required third-party notices.
blocking_findings.required_change: Pin exact SDK/esbuild versions, define reproducible lockfile inputs, preserve license notices and use isolated execution or syntax-aware inspection to prove no runtime SDK import remains.

non_blocking_findings.description: Removing the optional reuse question leaves no explicit replacement for the existing requirement to consider reuse before implementation.
non_blocking_findings.required_change: Assign the executor a conservative repository-local reuse check or require it to follow the existing recorded reuse decision without escalating an ordinary question.

non_blocking_findings.description: The statement that physical pane adjacency does not give reviewers access to each other's output is too strong in a shared Herdr session.
non_blocking_findings.required_change: State that independence is a prompt/process rule rather than an access-control boundary.

non_blocking_findings.description: Observed installed run does not define evidence that forbidden files were not read.
non_blocking_findings.required_change: Require an auditable orchestrator command interval or controlled access fixture.

assumptions: A recent provider session is not sufficient evidence of current successful unattended launch.
Terminal normalization prevents literal byte identity while still permitting an exact normalized-text invariant.
Bundled SDK JavaScript with a system provider executable remains compatible with the dependency-free shipped-helper contract.
